title: Handmade Sellers: The Photo Style That Justifies Premium Prices
description: Handmade sellers can charge 3x more with the right photo aesthetic. Here's how to shoot photos that justify premium prices.

blocks.text: Handmade buyers pay more—but only when your photos justify it. A hand-thrown ceramic mug photographed on a messy counter looks like a garage sale find. The same mug on curated linen looks like a $60 boutique piece.
Same product. 3x the price. All because of visual framing.
The Handmade Premium Aesthetic
Successful handmade sellers photograph products with:

items.text: Natural materials as backgrounds (wood, linen, stone)
Soft window light, never harsh flash

blocks.text: Nail this and buyers understand why you charge $60 for what a factory version sells for $15.

The Editing Magic
Handmade often means imperfect backgrounds. Your linen has wrinkles. Your wood has stains. Your table shows through.
Export a transparent PNG from edit-photo, then place it into the final scene or layout with a general design editor. Keep the original and transparent master so the composition remains reversible.

The Story Angle
Handmade buyers pay for story as much as product. Include:

items.text: A shot of the workspace (bench, wheel, easel)
A shot of hands working (blurred motion is fine)

blocks.text: These don't need editing perfection—they need authenticity. But make sure they're not accidentally cluttered.
